userScenario: Correct the first task of a planned project; continue its dependent step after the corrected result.
existingCapabilities: Durable scheduling, linked resumptions and recorded corrections already exist.
Earlier lifecycle test covers restart admission idempotency, dependency result transfer and chain cancellation.

probe.environment: Disposable PostgreSQL database; existing test container; schema created and disposable database removed by fixture.
observed: Dependent task scheduled after first work ID.
Correction saved and one resumption queued.
Scheduler permanently blocks dependent task against stopped original attempt.
Next scheduler pass admits corrected continuation.
probe.interpretation: Passing reproduction assertions confirm a defect, not successful project continuation.
limits: Controlled scheduler/service entry points; no conversation model or external task execution.
No real multi-day wait or generated artifact.
No source change or installation in this investigation.

cause: ScheduledOwnerWork._dependency loads the exact original work ID and treats its correction stop as terminal; it does not resolve the explicitly queued correction continuation. run_once persists this as blocked before that continuation can finish.
nextAction: Repair dependency resolution for explicitly recorded correction continuations, including the queued-before-admitted interval; preserve explicit chain cancellation, absence of a continuation, owner boundaries and one-time admission. Convert reproduction into expected continuation regression.

findings: Concrete continuation defect, not missing acceptance.
Follow only explicitly corrected continuation of same execution; preserve original dependency.
Correction stop/save/schedule use separate transactions: avoid premature blocking during this interval.
Explicit cancellation remains decisive; no blanket restart of blocked work.
review.scope: Independent source and recorded-output review; no repeated execution.
